# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 👌]

I see the bomb: a display showing 0, a red light, and three wires — 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Blind has gestured ☝ ✌ 👌 to me, which likely means "1 2 3" — probably referencing the wires. I can't hear anything, so I only have this gesture and my own view. I need to get information to Blind (who can touch the bomb) and Mute (who has the manual). Blind can't see my gestures, only hear my speech — but I can't speak to Blind directly in a way they'd perceive gestures... wait, Blind can hear speech (Blind can't see, but can hear). Mute can hear speech and see gestures. Deaf (me) can only gesture, and only Mute sees gestures. Blind hears my speech. So I should speak to Blind with my visual info, and gesture to Mute too.

Let me send my visual reading to Blind via speech, and also gesture to Mute since Mute sees gestures and hears speech — actually Mute hears my speech too. So speaking reaches both Mute and Blind. Gesturing reaches only Mute.

I'll speak my full visual: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. And gesture the same wire info to Mute in case.

Actually, I should be careful: Blind gestured 1 2 3 — maybe asking about wire order or which wire. I'll give my full view.

Let me speak to everyone (Mute and Blind hear it) and gesture to Mute the wire colors.

I'll send:
- speak(text="I see: display reads 0, light is red. Wires: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
- gesture to mute with symbols representing the colors? But colors have no gesture names necessarily. I can gesture numbers: ☝ ✌ 👌 already used. Maybe gesture wire numbers and something. But Mute already hears my speech, so gesture is redundant. I'll just speak.

Actually gesture could help emphasize. But no need. I'll speak to all.I see the bomb clearly: display shows 0, the light is red, and the three wires are 1=blue, 2=red, 3=green. Blind's gesture ☝✌👌 almost certainly means "1 2 3" — likely asking about or referring to the wires. Since Blind can hear speech but not see gestures, and Mute can both hear speech and see gestures, I'll speak my full visual reading so both Mute and Blind receive it. I'll also gesture the wire numbers to Mute as a backup, though Mute already hears me.

I have no manual and can't touch the bomb, so my job is to transmit my visual world accurately. I'll state everything plainly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is red. Wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green. I received your gesture 1 2 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is red. Wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green. Blind gestured 1 2 3 to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 👌]

Mute has gestured ✌ (2) to me, and Blind again gestured 1 2 3. The board is unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

Mute sees my gestures and hears my speech. Mute gesturing ✌ likely means "wire 2" — perhaps pointing at wire 2 (red) as relevant. Blind repeating 1 2 3 might be confirming the wire set or asking again.

I should acknowledge and perhaps clarify. Mute has the manual — Mute may be trying to tell me something about wire 2. But I can't hear Mute's speech; I only see gestures. Mute's gesture ✌ could mean "wire 2 is the one" or "second wire."

I should respond: confirm wire 2 is red, and ask/state what I know. Since I can only reach Mute via gesture and both via speech, I'll speak to both and gesture to Mute.

Let me gesture back to Mute acknowledging wire 2, and speak my view again for Blind's benefit.

I'll gesture: ✌ (2) and maybe point. And speak: "Wire 2 is red. Display 0, light red. What does the manual say?"

Actually I should be careful not to assume. I'll just relay and ask.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Still: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured 2 to me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is red. Display 0, light red. Please tell me what the manual says to do.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
```

Board unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

Mute again gestures ✌ (2). Blind now gestures ✌👌 (2 3).

Blind is now signaling 2 3 — maybe asking about wires 2 and 3, or indicating the relevant wires are 2 and 3. Mute keeps saying 2. Mute has the manual, so Mute's repeated ✌ likely means wire 2 is the key wire.

I should relay clearly and try to get the manual's instruction. Since I can't hear, I depend on Mute's gestures. Mute may be limited in what they can gesture. Let me confirm my view and gesture back.

I'll speak to both, and gesture to Mute: ✌ (2) and maybe ✌👌 to match Blind. Actually I should gesture what I know: wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.

Let me gesture to Mute: ✌ 👌 to indicate wires 2 and 3, and speak the colors.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute keeps gesturing 2; you gestured 2 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green, wire 1 is blue. Display 0, light red. What does the manual say? Which wire?")

```

LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed: light is now yellow, wire 2 is CUT, display still 0. Mute gestured 👍 — approval, meaning the wire 2 cut was correct. So the manual's instruction was to cut wire 2, and it worked.

Now the bomb has changed. New state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 blue, 2 cut, 3 green. I need to report this and get new guidance from Mute (manual) and Blind (hands).

I'll speak the new state to both, and gesture acknowledgment to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 2 cut was correct. Bomb changed: display still 0, light is now yellow. Wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 cut was correct. Bomb changed: display still 0, light is now yellow. Wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. What next?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Board: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

Mute gestures ☝ (1) — likely wire 1 is next. Blind gestures ☝👌 (1 3) — wires 1 and 3.

Mute's ☝ probably means cut wire 1 next. Blind's 1 3 might be asking about remaining wires.

I'll relay and confirm. Speak to both, gesture to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="State: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute gestured 1; you gestured 1 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 is blue, wire 3 is green, wire 2 already cut. Display 0, yellow light. Do I tell Blind to cut wire 1?")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]

Mute gestured 👍 again — approval. But wait, did Blind actually cut wire 1? The board still shows wire 1 as [blue], not [CUT]. So no cut happened yet. Mute's 👍 might be approving my plan, or confirming wire 1 is correct.

Board unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

Mute's 👍 likely means "yes, wire 1." Blind still gestures 1 3.

I should clearly instruct Blind to cut wire 1. Blind can hear my speech. Let me speak directly to Blind with the instruction, and confirm with Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1 now. It is the blue wire. Wire 2 is already cut, wire 3 is green. Display 0, yellow light.")
speak(to="mute", text="Telling Blind to cut wire 1. Confirm?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 cut was correct. Bomb changed: light is now blue, display still 0, wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

Only wire 3 remains. Mute gestures 👍.

I'll report the new state and likely the next move is wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 cut was correct. Bomb changed: display 0, light is now blue. Wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Only wire 3 remains.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 cut correct. Now display 0, blue light, only wire 3 (green) remains. Cut wire 3?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

Board: display 0, blue light, wires 1 cut, 2 cut, 3 green.

Mute gestures 👌 (OK) — confirming. Blind gestures 👌☝ — maybe "OK, wire 1"? Or "OK, one wire left."

Mute's 👌 likely means yes, cut wire 3. I'll instruct Blind to cut wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3 now. It is the green wire. Wires 1 and 2 are already cut. Display 0, blue light.")
speak(to="mute", text="Telling Blind to cut wire 3 (green). Confirm.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```
